name: digitalReferenceMaterialDocument
description: The root of a DRMD. It serves both document types, the RM certificate (for a CRM) and the product information sheet (for an RM), and holds administrative data, materials, property values and statements, followed by an optional comment, optional embedded documents and optional digital signatures. The document type is set by coreData/titleOfTheDocument; the requirements that differ between the two types (ISO 33401:2024, Table 1) are checked by the companion Schematron rules (drmd-business-rules.sch).

rules.description: [DRMD-001] Every DRMD document MUST declare a titleOfTheDocument in coreData, specifying either 'referenceMaterialCertificate' or 'productInformationSheet'.
[DRMD-002] Every DRMD document MUST contain at least one material entry in the materials catalogue (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.4, Name of the RM).
[DRMD-003] Every DRMD document MUST contain at least one properties block with measurement data (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.15, Property of interest).

[RMC-001] Reference Material Certificates MUST include a metrologicalTraceability statement formalizing the chain of comparisons linking certified results to SI base units or international calibration benchmarks (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.4, Metrological traceability: 'Mandatory' for RM certificate). This is not required for productInformationSheet documents.

[RMC-002] Reference Material Certificates MUST have at least one properties block with the attribute isCertified="true" containing certified property values (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.3, Property value and associated uncertainty: 'Mandatory' for RM certificate). A certificate without certified values is structurally invalid.
[RMC-003] Reference Material Certificates MUST include property values (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.3, Property value and associated uncertainty).

[RMC-005] Reference Material Certificates SHOULD document the measurement procedures used for certified properties (ISO 33401:2024, §5.4.2, Measurement procedures for non-operationally defined measurands: 'Recommended' for both document profiles).

[RMC-010] Reference Material Certificates MUST list responsible persons including the name and function of the RM producer's approving officer (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.5, Name and function of the RM producer's approving officer: 'Mandatory' for RM certificate, 'Optional' for product information sheet).

[RMC-012] In a Reference Material Certificate, at least one dcc:respPerson MUST state a dcc:role. ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.5 requires the name AND the function of the officer representing the RM producer who accepts responsibility for the contents of the certificate; RMC-010 checks that the respPersons list exists, and this rule checks that the function is actually recorded. The role may name the responsible organisational unit rather than a personal job title (§5.3.5, NOTE). The officer's name is required by dcc:respPerson itself and needs no separate rule.

[RMC-011] Reference Material Certificates MUST include a description for each material (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.2, Description of the material: 'Mandatory' for RM certificate, 'Recommended' for product information sheet).

[PIS-001] Product Information Sheets MUST NOT mark any properties block as isCertified="true". Only Reference Material Certificate documents (CRM) may contain certified property values. Setting isCertified="true" on a productInformationSheet document constitutes a misrepresentation of the material's metrological status and violates the ISO 33401:2024 distinction between RMs and CRMs.
[PIS-002] Product Information Sheets MUST include results where property values are assigned (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.15, Property of interest).

children.name: coreData
children.description: Core data about the document: its type (RM certificate or product information sheet), its unique identifier, its version, optional further identifiers, and its period of validity.

rules.description: [DRMD-012] Every DRMD document MUST specify a validity period or condition (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.8, Period of validity).

[DRMD-011] Every DRMD document MUST state its documentVersion in coreData (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.13, Document version: 'Mandatory' for both document profiles). A version number, an approval date, or both are acceptable, provided the value changes whenever the document content changes. This requirement is also enforced structurally by drmd.xsd; the rule is stated here so that a Schematron report covers ISO 33401:2024, Table 1 in full on its own.

children.name: uniqueIdentifier
children.description: A mandatory identifier of this DOCUMENT that is unique worldwide (a UUID is recommended). If the content is changed after issue, a new document with a new unique identifier is issued; the existing document is not edited. SCOPE NOTE (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.2.3): this element identifies the document, not the reference material. The unique identifier OF THE RM required by Section 5.2.3, typically a product code combined with a batch or lot number such as "NMIJ CRM 7305-a" or "ERM-AC110", is carried by materials/material/materialIdentifiers and is enforced by Schematron rule DRMD-016. Do not use this element for the RM identifier: one document may cover several materials, and the same material is described by successive document revisions.

children.name: documentVersion
children.description: A mandatory version string identifying the revision of this document. Enables tracking of document updates and ensures recipients can verify they hold the current version (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.2.13, Mandatory for both document profiles). Its presence is required by this XSD and is additionally asserted by the companion Schematron rule DRMD-011, so that a Schematron-only validation report also covers the requirement. A version number, an approval date, or both are acceptable; whichever form is chosen must change whenever the document content changes.

rules.description: [DRMD-011] Every DRMD document MUST state its documentVersion in coreData (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.13, Document version: 'Mandatory' for both document profiles). This requirement is also enforced structurally by drmd.xsd; the rule is stated here so that a Schematron report covers ISO 33401:2024, Table 1 in full on its own.

children.name: documentIdentifier
children.description: A general-purpose identifier: the scheme it belongs to (for example DOI, CAS or ROR), the identifier value itself, and an optional link where it can be looked up. The @id, @refId and @refType attributes allow other parts of the document to refer to it.

children.name: scheme
children.description: The naming system, registry or authority the identifier comes from (e.g., 'DOI', 'CAS', 'ROR'). It tells software how to interpret and look up the value.

children.name: value
children.description: The identifier exactly as issued within the scheme (e.g., '10.1000/182' or '7440-50-8'). Give only the identifier here, without descriptive text, so that it can be searched and matched.

children.name: link
children.description: An optional, persistent URL (preferably HTTPS) where the identifier can be looked up or verified.

children.name: validity
children.description: The period of validity of the document (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.2.8), given in one of three ways: valid until revoked, valid for a period after dispatch, or valid until a fixed date. Software can compare it with the current date, for example to warn before an expired material is used.

rules.description: [DRMD-012] Every DRMD document MUST specify a validity period or condition (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.8, Period of validity).

children.name: untilRevoked
children.description: The document stays valid until the producer withdraws or replaces it. Suitable for materials whose property values are not expected to change over time.

children.name: timeAfterDispatch
children.description: Validity counted from the date a unit is dispatched. Software can add the period to the dispatch date to obtain the end of validity for an individual unit.

children.name: dispatchDate
children.description: The optional date on which the unit was dispatched. Where a document is issued and signed for each shipment, this date may coincide with the time stamp of the signature.

children.name: period
children.description: A mandatory ISO 8601 duration format string (e.g., 'P3Y2M') stating the exact lifespan allotted for material use once dispatched.

children.name: specificTime
children.description: A fixed end date of validity (YYYY-MM-DD). After this date the producer no longer guarantees the stated property values.

children.name: referenceMaterialProducer
children.description: The reference material producer: the organisation responsible for the reference material and for this document (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.2.5). Holds its name, contact details, optional statements on electronic seals, signatures and time stamps, and optional organisation identifiers such as ROR.

children.description: The producer's contact details: name, and optionally e-mail, phone, fax and web link, plus the postal address in dcc:location. Typically city, postCode, street, streetNo and countryCode are given; postOfficeBox, state and positionCoordinates are added only where they apply.

rules.description: [DRMD-002] Every DRMD document MUST contain at least one material entry in the materials catalogue (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.4, Name of the RM).
[DRMD-007] Every material entry MUST include a name element (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.4, Name of the RM).

[DRMD-008] Each material entry MUST specify a minimumSampleSize whenever applicable to ensure representative sampling for homogeneity (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.7, Minimum sample size: 'Mandatory whenever applicable' for both document profiles).

[DRMD-016] Each material entry MUST carry at least one materialIdentifier giving the unique identifier of the reference material (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.3, Unique identifier of the RM: 'Mandatory' for both document profiles). The identifier must distinguish this RM from any other RM issued by the same producer; a product code, normally combined with a batch or lot number, satisfies this. Note that coreData/uniqueIdentifier identifies the DOCUMENT and does not satisfy §5.2.3, because one document may cover several materials and one material may be described by successive document revisions.

[PIS-005] Product Information Sheets SHOULD include a description for each material. While not mandatory for Product Information Sheets, material descriptions improve usability (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.2, Description of the material: 'Recommended' for product information sheet, 'Mandatory' for RM certificate).

children.name: materialIdentifiers
children.description: The identifiers of the reference material, for example product code and batch or lot number, used to match the document to the physical unit and to database records. PROFILE NOTE (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.2.3): this element carries the unique identifier OF THE RM, which is MANDATORY for both document profiles. The element is structurally optional in the XSD only to keep the two profiles on one content model; its presence is enforced by the companion Schematron rule DRMD-016 (error). Provide at least one identifier that distinguishes this RM from any other RM issued by the same producer, normally a product code and, where units are produced in batches, a batch or lot number as a second identifier. Where each unit is individually characterised, add the unit serial number as a further identifier. Keep the values exactly as they are printed on the container label, so that the physical unit and the document can be matched without interpretation.

children.name: materialIdentifier
children.description: A general-purpose identifier: the scheme it belongs to (for example DOI, CAS or ROR), the identifier value itself, and an optional link where it can be looked up. The @id, @refId and @refType attributes allow other parts of the document to refer to it.

rules.description: [DRMD-016] Each material entry MUST carry at least one materialIdentifier giving the unique identifier of the reference material (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.3, Unique identifier of the RM: 'Mandatory' for both document profiles). The identifier must distinguish this RM from any other RM issued by the same producer; a product code, normally combined with a batch or lot number, satisfies this. Note that coreData/uniqueIdentifier identifies the DOCUMENT and does not satisfy §5.2.3, because one document may cover several materials and one material may be described by successive document revisions.

children.name: scheme

children.name: value
children.description: The identifier exactly as issued within the scheme (e.g., '10.1000/182' or '7440-50-8'). Give only the identifier here, without descriptive text, so that it can be searched and matched.

children.name: link
children.description: An optional, persistent URL (preferably HTTPS) where the identifier can be looked up or verified.

children.name: propertiesList
children.description: The property values of the material, with units and uncertainties, grouped into blocks. Each block states with its @isCertified attribute whether its values are certified or informative.

children.name: properties
children.description: A block of property values: its name, an optional description, the measurement procedures, the results and optional metadata. The @isCertified attribute states whether the values in this block are certified ("true") or informative (attribute omitted or "false"). PROFILE NOTE (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.3): - referenceMaterialCertificate: MUST contain at least one properties block with @isCertified="true". Certified property values MUST include measurement uncertainty and metrological traceability (Schematron rules RMC-002, RMC-003). - productInformationSheet: MUST NOT set @isCertified="true" on any properties block. Uncertainty values are optional (Schematron rule PIS-001).

attributes.name: isCertified
attributes.description: States whether the values in this block are certified. "true" marks certified values. Omitted or "false" means the values are informative (not certified), for example indicative or additional values. INDICATIVE VALUES (ISO 33401:2024, Section 5.4.5, Optional for both document profiles): indicative values are carried in an ordinary properties block with isCertified omitted or set to 'false'. No separate element and no Schematron rule exist for them, because the requirement is optional. Give such a block a name that says what it holds (for example 'Indicative values') so that a reader and a parser reach the same conclusion as the attribute. PROFILE NOTE (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.3): - referenceMaterialCertificate: At least one properties block MUST have isCertified="true", and all certified property values MUST include expanded measurement uncertainty and metrological traceability. - productInformationSheet: isCertified MUST NOT be set to "true" on any properties block. This prevents informational RM documents from being misrepresented as certified data.

rules.description: [DRMD-003] Every DRMD document MUST contain at least one properties block with measurement data (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.15, Property of interest).
[DRMD-009] Every properties block MUST contain at least one result entry with measurement data (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.15, Property of interest).

[DRMD-014] Each properties block MUST include measurement procedures whenever applicable. This combines two ISO requirements: procedures for operationally defined measurands (ISO 33401:2024, §5.2.14, 'Mandatory whenever applicable' for both document profiles) and procedures for non-operationally defined measurands (ISO 33401:2024, §5.4.2, 'Recommended' for both document profiles). Taken together, the overall requirement is 'Mandatory whenever applicable'.

[RMC-002] Reference Material Certificates MUST have at least one properties block with the attribute isCertified="true" containing certified property values (ISO 33401:2024, §5.3.3, Property value and associated uncertainty: 'Mandatory' for RM certificate). A certificate without certified values is structurally invalid.

[PIS-003] In productInformationSheet documents, individual properties blocks MUST NOT have isCertified="true". This attribute should be omitted or set to "false" for all property blocks in a Product Information Sheet. Certified property values are only permitted in referenceMaterialCertificate documents.

It is available inside si:real and the list variants, and is recommended for every certified value: it tells a consumer what was measured, which a unit alone does not. A QUDT quantity kind is not a substitute for a unit and never replaces si:unit.

This supports long-term archiving, because a single XML file then holds both the machine-readable data and the human-readable document (see the "Archival Package" interoperability profile in the DRMD guidance document). Can also be used for embedding documents other than the RM document, or for multiple documents. Give each embedded document a name or description that says what it is, so that the rendition of the RM document can be told apart from any other file.

children.name: Signature
children.description: An optional, repeatable XML digital signature (XMLDSig) that lets a recipient check that the document has not been changed since it was signed, and who signed it. Note: the imported schema is the complete W3C XML Signature schema, so XSD validation does check the structure of the signature (SignedInfo and SignatureValue present, KeyInfo and Object optional, algorithm attributes present). What XSD validation cannot do is verify the cryptography: recomputing digests, checking the signature value, and validating the certificate chain and its revocation status require a dedicated XMLDSig library. A structurally valid ds:Signature is therefore never, on its own, evidence that the document is authentic.
